items.title: Randy Weston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I play the piano like I play because I had the human contact with Thelonious Monk, because I had the spiritual contact with Nat King Cole, who I never met.

ctx.x: Now, you had made a solo recording before the Montreal Jazz Festival. But more recently, you made the recording “Ancient Future.” How did you come to make that record?

That wonderful book that Dr. Wayne Chandler wrote, which says that in order for us to go ahead we have got to go back. It’s like…I’m sure we all have the same experience. Mom and Pop told us some things when we were younger which we either rejected or we didn’t understand. When we become older, “Oh! That’s what Pop meant! That’s what Mom meant!” That goes all the way, all the way back. The ancient Egyptians, they created a concept of music, which is based upon spiritual values. Each planet has got its own sound.…
Were you inspired by that book and by what that book said to you when you read it? Were you inspired by that book to make this particular record as a solo piano record?
